title: Towards a Greener Climate -- Analysis Based on 4M System

limitations: Symbol font did not survive OCR for several variables.

tasks: Task 1: Choose a GGDP calculation method with measurable climate impact
Task 2: Build a climate mitigation impact model
Task 3: Cost-benefit analysis of the GDP-to-GGDP switch
Task 4: In-depth analysis of one country (Brunei)
Task 5: Non-technical report to that country's leader

contributions.summary: Selects the Stjepanovic et al. GGDP formula because it covers both quantitative costs and opportunity costs.
Shows %DIF coefficient is about one third of the GDP coefficient in climate regressions.
Predicts world GDP and GGDP recovery in 2052 and 2055, climate recovery after 2075.
Brunei recovery by 2077, more than 20 years later than the world, consistent with resource dependence.

dependency_graph.handoff: %DIF series is the regressor for climate indicators
GGDP identity rewritten using EC and ECPGDP
Intersection model reapplied to Brunei data

assumptions.summary: No major economic shocks in the future.
Leaders can change goals and strive for them.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: 160 countries, World Bank, OECD, UN data, 1979-2019 for %DIF.
21 climate indicators from NASA and NOAA, classified into four normalization types.

models.summary: ECB: Cost-benefit with OLS, future intersection via ARIMA/GM/SVM.
BRN: Brunei scenario with resource exhaustion and recovery.

verification.summary: Regression R-squared 0.89-0.98 across five climate indicators.

results_trace.summary: %DIF explains about one third of climate change.
Replacement is friendly to gender equality and HDI, slightly raises income inequality.
Recovery years: world GDP 2052, GGDP 2055; climate after 2075.

writing_logic.summary: Abstract uses 'For the [X]' blocks aligned with the 4M system label.
Three-category survey, then 'we finally chose' with characteristic as the reason.
Cost headings (Intergenerational Equity, Regional Equity) and benefit headings (Sustainable Development, Economic Growth, Moderate Change).
'It is worth noting' introduces the unexpected result, then 'This is because' explains it.
Numbered strengths each with a one-word label and a paragraph.

language_observations.summary: 'For the Method / For the Model / For the Mould / For the Movement' is a catchy parallel that reads as four mission blocks.
'We pay attention not only to the pace, but also to the color of the economy' is a metaphor that closes the background.
Assumption-Justification pairs use bold claim then a nested narrative, like paper 425's Assumption-Explanation but with Justification as the label.
'we finally chose' signals the selection without hedging; the characteristic is named as the reason.
'about 1/3 of climate change' is stated twice: once from the table and once from the comparison with real-world UNEP data.
'It is worth noting that [surprise]. This is because [reason]' is a two-sentence surprise-then-explain pattern.
'In any case, fortunately' concedes uncertainty and then delivers the good news.
'Dear King of Brunei' opening, 'We strongly believe' closing, Firstly/Secondly/Thirdly policy structure.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: Choosing a formula that covers both quantitative and opportunity costs gives a richer signal than a simple subtraction.
Stating a concrete fraction (one third) rather than just a significance test makes the climate link memorable.
Picking a high-dependence country for the case study maximizes the policy drama and makes the recovery narrative compelling.

weaknesses.summary: Four welfare indicators cannot comprehensively reflect all aspects of social welfare.
Missing values in the EWM data bring some inaccuracy.
Regression and time-series predictions lose accuracy over long horizons.
Alpha is assumed at 5% without empirical calibration.

independent_extensions.summary: Calibrate alpha from historical reform episodes instead of assuming 5%.
Add the random shock term epsilon they suggest in Section 9.3.

candidate_rule_impacts.summary: A GGDP formula that separates quantitative cost from opportunity cost produces a cleaner %DIF signal.
Selecting an extreme-dependence country for the case study makes the policy recommendation more dramatic.

unresolved_questions.question: What is the exact carbon price used, and does it vary by year or country?
How is the 3-year lag for efficiency gains justified beyond the single citation to He et al.?
